analysis.title: PayPal Holdings (PYPL): 3Q26 Takeaways: Shares outperform on modestly better EPS outlook
key_insights: GS keeps PYPL at Sell. It expects roughly flat EBIT growth, with EPS growth coming mostly from buybacks, and stays cautious on competitive dynamics in online checkout.

Shares outperformed modestly after the print. GS attributes this to 2027 EPS commentary that implies EPS modestly ahead of consensus, and to constructive comments on U.S. branded checkout, where growth improved sequentially.

Offsetting factors: continued reinvestment in transaction margin weighs on both transaction margin dollars and EPS growth, Europe faces headwinds from tariffs, de minimis changes and competition, and part of the opex beat was a pull-forward of cost savings.
Timing mismatches between cost savings and reinvestment could push the opex growth run rate higher over the course of 2027.
Management said it is open to strategic M&A, potentially larger than small bolt-ons. GS says this could change how investors view the range of outcomes for strategic options.

3Q26 revenue was about $8.58bn, roughly 1% below Visible Alpha consensus of about $8.71bn. Transaction revenue was about $7.71bn, 1% below consensus, and OVAS revenue was $873mn against $881mn consensus.

Transaction margin was about $3.95bn, 2% above consensus. Non-GAAP operating income was about $1.61bn, 14% above street expectations. Non-GAAP opex excluding transaction expense was about $2.34bn against street at $2.42bn.
Adjusted EPS was $1.45 ($1.25 GAAP), roughly 11% ahead of consensus.
4Q26 guidance: slightly positive transaction margin dollars, non-GAAP effective tax rate of about 19-20%, non-GAAP EPS of $1.43 and GAAP EPS of $1.37.

FY26 guidance: about $15.7bn transaction margin dollars, mid-single-digit opex growth, about 19% tax rate, non-GAAP EPS of about $5.60 ($5.07 GAAP), FCF of $6.5bn+, buybacks of about $6bn and capex of about $1bn.
Management expects FY27 non-GAAP EPS growth roughly in line with 2026 (about 5-6%), with a similar financial composition to 2026.
GS raises its 12-month price target to $51 from $49, based on an unchanged ~8x P/E on Q5-Q8 estimates. The stock closed at $56.09, which implies 9.1% downside.

market_movers.rationale: GS raised the target to $51 from $49 on an unchanged ~8x P/E applied to Q5-Q8 estimates. It remains Sell on competitive dynamics in online checkout and expects flattish EBIT growth with EPS growth driven by buybacks.

PYPL 3Q26 reported: transaction margin ~$3.95bn (+2% vs consensus). Non-GAAP operating income ~$1.61bn (+14% vs street). Non-GAAP opex ex transaction expense ~$2.34bn vs street $2.42bn.
PYPL 3Q26 reported: adjusted EPS $1.45 non-GAAP / $1.25 GAAP, roughly 11% ahead of consensus. Adjusted net income ~$1.25bn.
PYPL 4Q26 company guidance: non-GAAP EPS $1.43, GAAP EPS $1.37, non-GAAP tax rate ~19-20%, transaction margin dollars slightly positive.
PYPL FY26 company guidance: non-GAAP EPS ~$5.60 ($5.07 GAAP), transaction margin dollars ~$15.7bn, opex growth mid-single digits, FCF $6.5bn+, buybacks ~$6bn, capex ~$1bn.
PYPL FY27 company commentary: non-GAAP EPS growth roughly in line with 2026 expectations (~5-6%). GS says this implies EPS modestly ahead of consensus.
GS estimates (new vs old): 2026E EPS $5.61 (from $5.34), 2027E $5.95 (from $5.92), 2028E $6.73 (from $6.59). 2025 EPS was $5.30.
risk_factors: Continued reinvestment in transaction margin weighs on transaction margin dollars and EPS growth.
Headwinds in Europe from tariffs, de minimis changes and competition.
Cost savings were pulled forward, and timing mismatches with reinvestment could raise opex growth in 2027.
GS upside risks to its Sell: improving macro, better adoption of new products and services, and an improving competitive environment.
Larger strategic M&A could change the range of outcomes for the company.

tension_points.bull_case: The market appreciated 2027 EPS commentary implying EPS modestly ahead of consensus. U.S. branded checkout growth improved sequentially, and 3Q26 adjusted EPS of $1.45 was about 11% above consensus.
tension_points.bear_case: Reinvestment in transaction margin weighs on growth, Europe has headwinds, some of the beat was pulled-forward cost savings, and GS expects flattish EBIT growth with EPS growth mostly from buybacks.
tension_points.what_invalidates: GS names upside risks as improving macro, better adoption of new products and services, and an improving competitive environment, but gives no specific level or event.
